The IIME Active ETF launch timeline is now resolved: the underlying mutual fund/Active ETF Series launched via press release on Jul 27, 2026, with the TSX "Opens the Market" ceremony held separately on Sep 18/26 — both dates now independently corroborated and consistent with each other rather than in tension. iA Clarington's overall AUM (>$26B, Jul 31/26) and iAGAM's firm-wide AUM ($156B, Jun 30/26) were both reconfirmed unchanged, with no fresher figures found. On tariffs, today's research adds size and nuance to the Sep 29/26 "loaded date" story: Canada's Sep 8/26 Phase 1 counter-tariffs are now sized at roughly C$27.6B (15/25/50% rate bands) in response to the US's 50% tariffs on ~$20B of Canadian goods after talks collapsed Aug 21-22/26, with the previously-flagged ~C$125B Phase 2 package still expected roughly 21 days later (around Sep 29/26); however, one source found today (date stamp inconsistent across snippets — flagged as unverified) suggests Canada may have quietly scaled back its counter-tariff follow-through on CUSMA-covered goods versus the "dollar-for-dollar" framing originally reported — this detail could not be independently confirmed today and should be treated cautiously. The parallel US import ban on Canadian dairy-adjacent products, alcohol and motorcycles/mopeds (effective Sep 29/26, via Section 338 executive orders signed Sep 8/26) is reconfirmed with more legal specificity today. On Bombardier: today's research adds that Trump's threat (~Sep 7-8/26) to block US jet sales absent domestic manufacturing drew pushback from a Republican senator, and follows an earlier, unrealized threat from January 2026 (decertification/50% aircraft tariffs) — useful pattern-recognition context suggesting this kind of threat has not previously materialized. No fresh September-dated, allocation-specific PIMCO commentary was found; Loomis Sayles has Sep 14/26 and Sep 18/26-dated insight pieces (Solvency II reform; an EM credit/FX monthly review) whose full content could not be retrieved today.
